reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel sigma-algebra. Let gamma_E be the centered Gaussian probability measure on E with covariance the identity. Let L^2(gamma_E; R) be the real Hilbert space of square-integrable real-valued functions modulo gamma_E-almost-everywhere equality. Write H_j for the unnormalized probabilists' Hermite polynomial of degree j, with its integer coefficients interpreted in R (H_0(t)=1, H_1(t)=t, and H_(n+1)(t)=t H_n(t)-n H_(n-1)(t) for n>=1). Define Phi_j(w)=[x |-> H_j(<w,x>)] in L^2(gamma_E; R), where brackets denote the almost-everywhere equivalence class of the literal square-integrable function displayed. For every j in N={0,1,2,...}, the map Phi_j:E -> L^2(gamma_E; R) is twice continuously Frechet differentiable over R on the entire ambient space E. Differentiability is with respect to w and measured in the L^2 norm in the codomain.
domains: j in N; parameter w in all of E; output in L^2(gamma_E; R).
quantifiers: For every admissible E and every j in N, Phi_j is C^2 on E.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional real inner-product structure and Borel measurable structure only.
conclusion: ContDiff R 2 Phi_j, namely global C^2 regularity in the L^2 norm.
scopes: Ambient Frechet regularity in w, with no unit-sphere restriction and no differentiation in x asserted.
constant_dependencies: The map depends on E with its inner product and j; no numerical derivative bounds or auxiliary constants are quantified.
semantic_notes: The conclusion in this packet has order exactly 2; it does not state infinite smoothness.
The codomain is the actual L^2 equivalence-class space.
